review_method: Read all ten pinned original modules and compared their public and private capability contracts with the referenced Rust implementations.
Read the actual test assertions used for each behavioral group; native/source names below identify executable cases rather than merely mentioning a matching filename.
Private callbacks, source classes and context-manager plumbing are mapped to their real typed/recursive/owned native equivalents with a per-capability adaptation reason.

Validated exact105 old-ID set equality, native definition locations and named test references against the current worktree; did not execute the full test matrix again for this documentation-only review.
review_limits: Capability references establish concrete implementation and assertion coverage, not proof that every possible input or network service has been exercised.
Source-case test IDs retain the immutable inventory; related original cases may assert several fused helpers together. They are references to existing cases, not newly authored tests.
Existing tests often compare actual Rust operations against immutable original observations. No Python interpreter or hidden Python program is required by those native tests.

Authored application behavior now resides in browser-page-rust. Generated JavaScript is a transparent Rust compiler artifact with fixed tool/source/output attribution; original script text remains only in immutable characterization observations, not in product execution.

unverified_or_adapted_edges.detail: Source dataclass-reflection audit helpers are native test-time set comparisons against actual serialized Profile/Fingerprint/Proxy values and checked policy data. They are not exposed as a new production reflection API. Mutation assertions cover new, removed and unexplained fields.
An unstarted native Relay cannot be constructed. Relay::start returns only after readiness; stable URL access and idempotent close replace a repeated start call/property-before-start exception.
Malformed relay requests preserve400status and cleanup but use a static native detail instead of the source parser-specific body suffix. Exact suffix equivalence is not established.
Existing tests fault explicit bounded close/retry, and normal scope ownership is exercised. No separately faulted Drop-only stderr assertion is claimed.

The original source explicitly uses a plain TCP first hop for an https-labeled proxy. Native Upstream::connect preserves that behavior; this is not evidence of TLS encryption to an upstream HTTPS proxy.
